questions.question: Which of the following lists contains only essential food groups required by the human body?
options: Proteins, carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals
Glucose, carbon dioxide, water, and oxygen
Toxins, fiber, enzymes, and hormones
Lipids, proteins, lactic acid, and starch

questions.question: Why might an individual require different amounts of particular nutrients at different times in their life?
options: Because their genetic code changes as they grow older
To adapt to changing nutritional needs based on growth, pregnancy, or lifestyle
Because the energy value of a single gram of carbohydrate changes over time
To match the changing temperature of the external environment

questions.question: During an experiment to investigate the energy content of food, how is the energy released from burning food measured?
options: By measuring the increase in mass of the food sample
By measuring the volume of oxygen gas produced
By measuring the temperature change of a known volume of water
By calculating the amount of carbon dioxide released into the air

questions.question: Using the formula: Energy (J) = mass of water (g) x rise in temperature (°C) x 4.2, how much energy is transferred if 10 g of water rises in temperature by 5 °C?
options: 50 Joules
210 Joules
42 Joules
21 Joules

questions.question: In addition to acting as building materials for growth and repair, what role does food play in cellular respiration?
options: It provides the fuel to release energy for life processes
It acts as a cooling agent to reduce body temperature
It directly absorbs carbon dioxide from the blood
It eliminates the body's requirement for oxygen

questions.question: What information is typically provided on food labels to help consumers maintain a healthy diet?
options: The exact location where the crops were harvested
The content of the food and the daily recommended amounts of nutrients and energy
The total volume of oxygen used to package the food
The chemical structure of every single molecule in the food

questions.question: Which two units are commonly used on food labels to compare the amount of energy provided by different foods?
options: Joules and Newtons
Calories and grams
Kilojoules or calories
Watts or kilograms

questions.question: Which two physical measurements are required to calculate a person's Body Mass Index (BMI)?
options: Height and body mass
Waist circumference and heart rate
Age and physical activity level
Body mass and lung capacity

questions.question: What is the likely physical consequence of regularly consuming significantly more food and energy than the body needs?
options: The body mass index will decrease, eventually leading to starvation
The body mass index will become too high, leading to obesity
The body's rate of cellular respiration will permanently drop to zero
The resting heart rate will immediately decrease to healthy levels

questions.question: Obesity is a health condition that can significantly increase the risk of developing which of the following medical issues?
options: Scurvy
Heart disease
Infectious flu
Rickets

questions.question: What is the term for a health condition that is caused specifically by not consuming enough of a particular nutrient?
options: Infectious disease
Genetic disease
Deficiency disease
Environmental disease

questions.question: What does the term 'recovery time' refer to when assessing physical fitness after exercise?
options: The time it takes to complete a specific distance or task
The duration of exercise required to double the resting pulse rate
The time it takes for the heart rate to return to its resting rate after exercise
The total hours of sleep required after a physical workout

questions.question: How does a person's physical fitness level typically affect their recovery time after vigorous exercise?
options: People who are fitter have a shorter recovery time
People who are fitter have a longer recovery time
Fitness level has no impact on recovery time
People who are fitter do not experience an increase in heart rate during exercise

questions.question: In an experiment investigating how different types of exercise affect heart rate, which variables should be controlled?
options: The heart rate of the person after exercising
The person doing the exercise and the length of time spent exercising
The type of exercise performed by the participant
The outside weather temperature and the time of year

questions.question: When plotting a bar chart to show how different exercises affect heart rate, where should the dependent variable go?
options: On the x-axis
On the y-axis
In the title of the graph only
In a separate key on the side of the chart

questions.question: Why do breathing rate and heart rate increase when a person undergoes physical exercise?
options: To reduce the amount of water vapor in the lungs
Because cells need more oxygen for cellular respiration
To prevent carbon dioxide from entering the bloodstream
Because the body is trying to decrease its core temperature
